items.question: Why does baud mismatch cause garbage data?
items.answer: UART has no shared clock. The receiver samples each bit using its own timing. When baud rates differ, the sampling point slowly drifts, eventually causing bit errors.

items.question: Why does a small baud mismatch sometimes still work?
items.answer: With small baud differences, timing drift is slow. Early bits are sampled correctly, but errors appear only after several bits or characters.

items.question: Why does corruption appear in the middle of characters?
items.answer: Timing error accumulates over time. Early bits align correctly, but later bits drift into adjacent bit windows, causing corrupted data.

items.question: Why is the stop bit important?
items.answer: The stop bit forces the line HIGH, giving the receiver time to re-synchronize before the next character begins.

items.question: What happens on the line when no data is sent?
items.answer: When idle, the UART line stays HIGH. This idle state helps the receiver detect the next start bit reliably.
